headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance

CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.
